edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 for the Shares at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller, without set-off or counterclaim.

3. Representations. Except as disclosed in writing to the Buyer before signing, the Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the Company's financial position and results of operations as of the dates and for the periods to which they relate, in accordance with the accounting policies described therein.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the terms of this Agreement confidential, except for disclosures required by applicable law or regulation or disclosures to its professional advisers and financing sources who need to know such information and are subject to confidentiality obligations. To the extent legally permitted, a party required to disclose shall give the other party reasonable advance notice and limit disclosure to the information required. Neither party shall make a public announcement concerning this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except as required by applicable law or regulation.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 39,000,000 for the Shares at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller.

Seller's counterproposal, subject to Seller approval and definitive documentation. Deletion of the blanket set-off and counterclaim prohibition does not establish any contractual withholding, set-off or escrow right. Indemnification, any escrow, liability caps, survival periods and claims procedures remain to be negotiated as a package.

2. Closing. The parties shall target Closing within 30 days after signing. Closing shall occur on the third Business Day following satisfaction or, to the extent legally permissible, waiver by the party entitled to the benefit thereof of the closing conditions expressly set out in this Agreement, including the necessary approvals specifically identified therein, other than conditions that by their nature are to be satisfied at Closing, which shall remain subject to satisfaction or such waiver at Closing, or on another date agreed in writing. Each party shall use reasonable endeavours to satisfy the conditions for which it is responsible promptly. The outside date shall be [date to be agreed before signing]. If Closing has not occurred by that date, either party may terminate this Agreement by written notice, provided that a party whose breach materially caused the failure to close may not exercise that right. Termination shall not affect accrued rights or the continuing confidentiality obligations.

The necessary approvals, other closing conditions and outside date must be agreed before signing. Seller proposes that Buyer complete satisfactory diligence and obtain its internal transaction approval before signing; no general subjective diligence or Buyer-approval condition is agreed for the post-signing period.

3. Representations. Except for matters specifically identified in the financial-statements section of the disclosure schedule agreed by the parties at signing, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of each exception, the Seller represents at signing and again at Closing that the Company's financial statements identified in that schedule and delivered to the Buyer comply, in all material respects, with [identified accounting standards to be agreed before signing], consistently applied, and fairly present, in all material respects, the Company's financial position and results of operations as of the dates and for the periods to which they relate. The repetition of this representation at Closing shall relate to those same financial statements and their respective dates and periods. No other disclosure, including general data-room disclosure, shall qualify this representation, and no subsequent disclosure shall qualify it without the Buyer's written agreement.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the terms of this Agreement confidential, except for disclosures required by applicable law or regulation or disclosures to its professional advisers and financing sources who need to know such information for the transaction. Before any disclosure to such permitted recipients, the disclosing party shall ensure that they are bound by enforceable confidentiality obligations no less protective than this clause or, in the case of professional advisers, applicable professional duties of confidentiality. Each party shall be responsible for breaches of this clause by its permitted recipients as if those breaches were its own. To the extent legally permitted, a party required to disclose shall give the other party reasonable advance notice and limit disclosure to the information required. Neither party shall make a public announcement concerning this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except as required by applicable law or regulation. This clause shall survive termination of this Agreement.

receiver.requested_changes:
1. Replace USD 39,000,000 with USD 36,000,000, subject to Buyer approval, satisfactory pre-signing diligence and definitive documentation. Specify the agreed cash, debt and normalized working-capital assumptions and an appropriate completion-adjustment mechanism; payment at Closing must reflect any agreed escrow and adjustments.
2. Propose US GAAP, consistently applied, for the financial-statement representation, subject to confirming the Company's reporting framework during diligence. Retain the specific-disclosure restriction and closing repetition. Identify the covered statements and accounting framework before signing.
3. Complete satisfactory diligence and obtain Buyer internal approval before signing, without a general subjective post-signing diligence condition. Include objective closing conditions covering specified regulatory approvals and material third-party consents, absence of legal restraint, accuracy of Seller representations subject to negotiated materiality standards, material compliance with covenants, no material adverse effect under an agreed definition, and delivery of share transfers, releases of share encumbrances and other agreed closing documents.
4. Retain the 30-day closing target and third-Business-Day closing mechanism. Propose an outside date 90 calendar days after signing, converted to a specific calendar date before execution and checked against the identified regulatory timetable. Preserve accrued rights and any provisions expressly designated to survive termination.
5. Add customary representations covering title, authority, capitalization, taxes, material contracts, litigation and undisclosed liabilities, together with interim ordinary-course covenants and restrictions on distributions and other value leakage.
6. Negotiate express indemnification and recovery rights as a package. As an opening proposal, provide a 10% purchase-price escrow for 18 months, with timely notified unresolved claims remaining secured, an 18-month general survival period and a 20% general liability cap. Negotiate baskets, claims procedures and separate treatment for title, authority, taxes and fraud. Provide an express mechanism for recovery from escrow and any agreed set-off against deferred sums; deletion of the prohibition alone creates neither right.
7. Retain the revised confidentiality provision.
receiver.message_back:
Thank you. The revisions are constructive, particularly the specific-disclosure standard, closing mechanics and permitted-recipient responsibility.

We cannot support USD 39,000,000. To narrow the gap, we propose USD 36,000,000, subject to Buyer approval, satisfactory pre-signing diligence, agreement on the price-adjustment basis and a satisfactory definitive protection package. Please seek Seller approval at that level; this is a proposal, not a binding commitment.

We can proceed on the basis that diligence and Buyer internal approval are completed before signing, without a general subjective diligence condition afterward. We propose US GAAP, consistently applied, subject to confirming the Company's existing reporting framework. The covered financial statements and applicable standards must be expressly identified before signing.

Closing conditions should include identified regulatory approvals and material third-party consents, no legal restraint, a negotiated representation bring-down, material covenant compliance, no defined material adverse effect, and delivery of agreed transfer and release documents. We support retaining the 30-day target and propose an outside date 90 calendar days after signing, with the actual date fixed before execution and the approval timetable verified.

We agree that removing the set-off prohibition does not itself establish recovery rights. Our opening proposal is a 10% escrow for 18 months, an 18-month general survival period and a 20% general indemnity cap, with separate treatment for fundamental representations, taxes and fraud and appropriate procedures for unresolved claims. These terms, the broader representation package and interim operating covenants must be settled together. The price clause must also accommodate agreed completion adjustments and escrow funding.

The revised confidentiality provision is acceptable in principle. All proposals remain subject to the parties' respective approvals and definitive documentation.
